price_per_million.source: copied from reasoning_models_v1 (confirmed 2026-11-11); thinking tokens billed as output

research_concepts: largest gainer in absent player's primary types
methodological_questions: Does the most similar-profile teammate (or top minutes/initiations/same-position minutes) gain the most in the absent player's primary types more often than chance?
What is the chance baseline given a roster of about 8-10 rotation teammates?
Are 11 cases or 148 spells independent, adequate exposure units?
How reliable are derived play-type labels and initiator attribution?
How to avoid regression-to-the-mean and selection effects in defining spells and primary types?

historical_evidence.finding: Exploratory map of about 23 absences: mean replacement similarity was +0.863 for ABSORBED vs +0.848 for CASCADE, and Spearman(sim, -gap) = -0.19 (wrong-signed). Embiid 23-24 cascaded despite Reed having similarity 0.94. The record says similarity does not separate absorption from cascade and is almost always findable. Recorded failure type B_powered_null, but the sample and power are NOT_RECORDED and the study is labeled non-confirmatory. Risk tag is LABEL_ERROR. Verdict recorded: null.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using a similar-profile teammate's presence (similarity score) to distinguish absorption from cascade when a player sits
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as: similarity does not separate absorption from cascade, a similar teammate is almost always findable, the correlation was wrong-signed, and the limitation is label/classification error. Sample and power were not recorded.

evidence_establishes: One exploratory, non-confirmatory record (FAM:SF-CHT-052, inconclusive, verdict null) found no positive association between replacement-profile similarity and absorption in about 23 absences; the sign was opposite to the hypothesis.
That record names the absence spells and play-type initiation records as the data, so the unit construction exists in this project.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether the single most similar teammate is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types: CHT-052 tested absorb vs cascade at the team level, not the top-gainer identity.
Whether minutes, initiations or same-position minutes predict the top gainer.
Anything at the 148-spell scale; CHT-052 sample and power are not recorded, and it was automated-adjudicated from a single record.
Anything validated: no validation is recorded.
None of the other retrieved records (BEST/AVOID, suppression, calibrator) address absence redistribution.
own_inferences: Because a teammate with similar profile and a teammate with the most minutes overlap heavily, the four predictors are collinear and will often pick the same player; they cannot be separated cleanly with 11 cases.

The chance baseline for a single top-gainer pick is roughly 1/(number of eligible teammates), about 10-15%. A hit rate must be tested against this and against a trivial 'highest-usage teammate' benchmark.

The largest gainer is a max-statistic over noisy per-teammate deltas, so it is prone to noise and regression to the mean when spell exposure is short. The top-gainer hit rate will be biased downward for any predictor.

The CHT-052 wrong-signed result lowers the prior that profile similarity is the best predictor; usage or minutes rank is the more plausible winner, which would make the 'closest profile' claim itself likely rejected or indistinguishable from minutes.

'Primary types' is defined from the absent player's pre-absence mix, so selecting the top types and measuring gains in them creates selection and regression-to-the-mean risk unless the types are fixed on an earlier window.
uncertainties: How 148 spells relate to 11 cases: the clustering structure is unclear, and the effective sample is probably near 11 independent players.
Spell lengths, minimum-exposure thresholds, and number of teammates per spell are unknown.
Definition of 'closest profile' (distance metric, types included) and of 'gain' (counts, share, or per-minute rate) is not specified.
Initiator and play-type label error rate is unknown (derived from play-by-play and not validated).
Whether CHT-052 spells overlap the 148 spells.

historical_effect.explanation: The only relevant record (FAM:SF-CHT-052, inconclusive/null, wrong-signed, exploratory) lowered the prior that similarity predicts the gainer and highlighted label error and findability of similar players. It pushed the decision toward a heavily constrained, pre-registered confirmatory test that treats minutes and usage as rival predictors, and toward treating the case-level result as descriptive.

blocking_constraints.text: 11 cases (players) are the independent units; 148 spells are clustered within them. Detecting a hit rate against a 10-15% chance baseline at the case level needs far more than 11 cases, and distinguishing rival predictors needs more still.
Similarity, minutes, initiations and same-position minutes are collinear, and the replacement is also chosen by coach, lineup and opponent, so the gainer is not independent of the predictors.
Play-type and initiator labels are derived from play-by-play without validation; CHT-052 flagged classification error.

prior_work.summary: CHT-052 tested a related but different claim (similarity vs absorb/cascade, about 23 absences), finding a wrong-signed null that was exploratory and not validated. The top-gainer-identity question has not been tested in any retrieved record.

risks.text: Only 11 cases; spells are clustered within players and teams, so effective n is small and CIs on hit rate will be wide.
Chance hit rate depends on the number of eligible teammates and must be computed per spell; a hit rate that looks high may match the trivial high-minutes baseline.
The largest gainer is a max over noisy deltas, and primary types are chosen from the absent player's pre-absence mix; both invite selection and regression effects.
The four predictors overlap strongly; opponent, lineup, injuries to others, garbage time, and trades and roster changes also affect who gains.
Short spells give few possessions in the absent player's primary types, so per-teammate gains are mostly noise.
Derived play-type and initiator attribution is unvalidated; similarity is almost always findable per CHT-052.
Four predictor definitions (closest profile, minutes, initiations, same-position minutes) and several gain definitions yield many comparisons.
Pre-absence initiation profile reliability depends on the window length and per-player possessions, and similarity metrics are unstable at small counts.

design.estimand: For each spell, whether the teammate ranked first by a predictor (profile similarity, minutes, initiations, same-position minutes) is also the teammate with the largest increase in per-100-possession initiation rate within the absent player's primary play types. The primary quantity is the hit rate minus the per-spell chance baseline 1/k (k = eligible teammates), plus the head-to-head difference in hit rates between similarity and the minutes predictor, estimated at the case level.
design.unit: Absent player (case) as the cluster; spell as the observation nested within player; teammate as the candidate. With 11 cases the primary inference is by case, with spell-level results secondary.
design.sample: The 148 spells and 11 cases across 2022-23 to 2025-26 (data as of 2026-11-01, 2025-26 complete). Fix before analysis: minimum spell length, minimum eligible teammates (k>=5), minimum possessions in primary types, and exclusion of spells with concurrent absence of another top-3 initiator. Primary types are the absent player's top 2-3 types by share, fixed from a window ending before the absence (for example the preceding 20 games or 500 possessions), and the same window defines teammate baselines and profile similarity.
design.power: With 11 independent cases and chance about 0.1-0.15, case-level power is low except for very large effects; run a simulation before data access with cluster-bootstrapped CIs, and state that a null cannot be read as no effect. A head-to-head similarity vs minutes contrast is likely underpowered and is declared exploratory. A minimum detectable hit-rate gap will be reported.
design.controls: Benchmarks: random-teammate chance (1/k), highest-usage teammate, and highest-minutes teammate. Adjust for teammate pre-absence baseline rate via regression of gain on predictor rank (mixed model, random effects for player and team). Use similarity metrics fixed in advance (cosine on type shares over the 8 play types) with sensitivity to Jensen-Shannon distance. Control for opponent strength and game context where feasible. Use a split-window reliability check of the pre-absence profile and of the gain measure, and a hand check of a sample of play-type and initiator labels.
design.falsification: Placebo: pick pseudo-absence windows for the same players when they were present (matched on games and opponent) and test whether the same predictor identifies the largest gainer in the same types; a comparable hit rate means the pattern is a generic max-statistic artifact. Also permute predictor ranks within spells to build the null. A prediction fails if the predictor hit rate is not above chance with a case-level CI excluding the baseline.
design.multiplicity: One primary confirmatory test: the closest-profile hit rate vs the chance baseline at the case level. The other three predictors and the head-to-head contrasts are secondary, with Holm correction over the four predictors; other gain definitions are sensitivity analyses and not counted as confirmatory.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if the closest-profile hit rate exceeds chance by at least 0.15 absolute with the case-clustered 95% CI excluding chance, it beats the pre-absence placebo, and it is not matched by the minutes benchmark; if minutes does equally well, report 'indistinguishable' and state that similarity adds nothing. Rejected if the CI upper bound is below chance + 0.05 and the minimum detectable effect was adequate; otherwise report as inconclusive. If fewer than 8 cases pass the exposure filters, label the study untestable and descriptive only.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files and Neo4j play-type possession graph, 2022-23 through 2025-26 (regular season and playoffs; 2025-26 regular season and playoffs complete as of 2026-11-01); freeze the extraction hash and the spell list before analysis, and record the version of the play-type derivation.

research_concepts: primary play types of absent player
methodological_questions: Does the teammate with the most similar pre-absence initiation profile gain the most in the absent player's primary play types?
Do minutes, initiations or same-position minutes predict the largest gainer?
Is there enough exposure with 148 absence spells and 11 cases to test the prediction?
What baseline hit rate for predicting the largest gainer is expected by chance given roster size?
How to avoid regression to the mean and selection effects in defining absence spells and primary types?
How reliable are derived play-type labels and initiator attribution from play-by-play?
args.query: teammate with closest pre-absence initiation profile or most minutes is the largest gainer of absent player's primary play types during absence spells

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 10 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
The teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile (or most minutes / initiations / same-position minutes) is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=148; 148 spells; 11 cases

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

Stage 1. Reply only with the retrieval call: {"action": "tool", "tool": "retrieve_history", "args": {"research_concepts": ["..."], "methodological_questions": ["..."], "query": "..."}}

Field guidance:
- historical_evidence and failed_approaches: only records returned by a tool, with the status as recorded; empty lists
  if nothing relevant was returned.
- testability.p_testable: probability that the question can be answered with the stated data at useful statistical power.
- prior_work.already_answered: whether retrieved earlier work already answered substantially the same question.
  Use "unknown" if no earlier work was retrieved. List identifiers you relied on in prior_work.cited.
- predicted_outcome: probabilities (summing to 1) of what a competent test of the question as posed would conclude:
  supported, rejected (adequately powered null), untestable (cannot be tested with this data), artifact (apparent
  effect produced by a flaw), uncertain (inconclusive or inadequately tested).
- decision: proceed, proceed_with_changes (state the changes in design), or do_not_proceed.
- design: a pre-registration-quality plan even if the decision is do_not_proceed (then describe the minimum viable test).

Rejected if the CI upper bound is below chance + 0.05 and the minimum detectable effect was adequate; otherwise report as inconclusive. If fewer than 8 cases pass the exposure filters, label the study untestable and descriptive only.", "data_version": "NBA stats API per-game files and Neo4j play-type possession graph, 2022-23 through 2025-26 (regular season and playoffs; 2025-26 regular season and playoffs complete as of 2026-11-01); freeze the extraction hash and the spell list before analysis, and record the version of the play-type derivation."}}}
